title: Titanium Hex Nut (ISO 4032)
alloyReason: Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5) offers the best balance of high strength (yield >830 MPa), excellent fatigue resistance, and corrosion resistance for precision-machined components. Its strength-to-weight ratio is 45% better than steel, making it the most widely used titanium alloy in aerospace, medical, and industrial applications.
commonFailures: Thread galling (cold welding) when titanium threads mate without anti-seize compound
Torque stripping of internal hex drive from shallow broaching or soft material
Hydrogen embrittlement in cathodic protection environments if Fe content exceeds limits

faq.q: What is a titanium hex nut (iso 4032)?
faq.a: A titanium hex nut (iso 4032) is a precision-machined fastener component used in heavy hex nut m12-m30 (grade 2 cp-ti). Manufactured from Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V for optimal strength, corrosion resistance, and weight savings.

faq.q: What is the typical application for titanium hex nut (iso 4032)?
faq.a: Titanium Hex Nut (ISO 4032) is designed for heavy hex nut m12-m30 (grade 2 cp-ti). The Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V grade is selected to provide the optimal balance of strength, fatigue life, and environmental resistance for this specific application.

faq.q: How is titanium hex nut (iso 4032) manufactured?
faq.a: Titanium Hex Nut (ISO 4032) is manufactured using Cold heading. Critical process controls include tool path optimization, coolant temperature management, and dimensional verification at each operation.

faq.q: What is the most common issue with titanium hex nut (iso 4032)?
faq.a: The most common issue is thread galling (cold welding) when titanium threads mate without anti-seize compound. Mitigation includes proper process control, material certification, and adherence to recommended installation procedures and torque values.
